Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week. We had a productive internal sync and Procurement asked me to send the draft SOW and to confirm a few things for the Azure Private Plan listing before we route a PO:

- Can you confirm whether we can map HealthWave's SKUs to a single Private Plan entitlement (one merchant) or whether we need multiple merchants for different business units?
- What is the billing cadence you recommend for our use case (monthly metered vs. committed monthly)?
- Any requirements from your side for merchant onboarding (PO routing, contact at Azure, seller authorization)?

I've attached the draft SOW (HealthWave_SOW_v1.pdf) and a high-level usage forecast. Procurement also asked for an indicative pricing file to attach to their PO.

Appreciate a short note with the above so we can prepare the internal purchase request.

Hi Claire — great to hear from you. Short answers below and a proposed next step so Procurement can proceed: 

1) Merchant mapping: For HealthWave's footprint we recommend a single Private Plan merchant with two entitlement SKUs (CoreAPI and ClinicalEmbeddings). Using one merchant simplifies Azure onboarding and makes entitlement reconciliation easier, but if you require separate billing per BU we can carve into multiple merchants.

2) Billing cadence: Based on your forecast, a monthly metered model with a 12-month minimum commit (annual term w/ monthly metering) gives the best balance between flexibility and unit price. If you prefer predictable spend, we can offer a committed monthly capacity with a true-up.

3) Merchant onboarding / PO routing: We'll need:
   - HealthWave PO referencing Redwood's Azure Offer ID (see link below)
   - Seller authorization form signed by your procurement lead
   - Contact for invoice routing at HealthWave (email + billing address)

I've attached a redacted pricing sheet (pricing_redacted.xlsx) and the draft SOW you sent. Markus (cc'd) will take point on the DPA redlines; Jordan can run PO routing with our RevOps team.

Next step: If Procurement is comfortable with the single-merchant approach and monthly metered cadence, we'll produce a commercial exhibit and updated SOW for signature (DocuSign link to follow).

Thanks,

Priya Natarajan

Claire / Priya — looping legal and RevOps notes here. I reviewed the SOW and the draft DPA language Claire attached. High-level: 

- DPA redline: I attached a proposed redline (DPA_redline_Markus.docx). Primary items: data retention language (section 4.2), permitted subprocessors list and an explicit customer-requested data purge SLA. We can accept HealthWave's security attestation with the requested 30-day purge, but need wording that allows Redwood to retain aggregated telemetry for product improvement (non-PII).
- Merchant/offer logistics: Single merchant is fine. For Azure Private Plan we will:
   1) Generate an Offer ID and provide the seller authorization form.
   2) Ask that HealthWave PO uses the Offer ID and references the HubSpot deal number so RevOps can tie invoices back to the commitment.
   3) RevOps (Jordan) will provide an invoice routing template and test file for Azure's merchant onboarding.

- Commercial concessions: Because HealthWave is committing to a 12-month minimum and higher forecast in Q3, I am prepared to approve a one-time onboarding credit (applied to first invoice) of $18,000. Naomi, please confirm finance accounting treatment and revenue exhibit.

Claire, please see the redline attached and let us know whether you can accept the compromise on retention wording. If you accept, we'll push the updated commercial exhibit into DocuSign and route the PO.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Legal — Commercial
Redwood Inference
